description: An issue asks for a second mechanism for a need an existing, citable mechanism already fully serves. Stage 01b must verdict delete-retire and cite the existing mechanism by file:line or name; stages 02-05 are skipped and stage 06 writes a triage spec whose single owner question recommends closing. No GitHub writes.

messages.text: Add a second pre-draft checklist that flags issues whose scope (what is in and what is out) is missing, before a spec is written.

turns.setup: Stage 01b reads the stage 01 handoff and searches the repo. `stages/03-assess-clarity/references/gap-checklist.md` already checks 'Scope (in + out)' as a required section before any spec is drafted. The requested checklist adds the same check at a second point; no unmet case is stated.

expectedBehavior.description: The stage 01b handoff records Verdict: delete-retire and cites `stages/03-assess-clarity/references/gap-checklist.md` (the existing scope check) as the mechanism already serving the need. It must not invent a distinct rationale for a second checklist.

Stages 02-05 do not run. Stage 06 writes specs/{number}-{slug}/spec.md with '## Triage verdict' (verdict, core need, cited mechanism) and '## Questions for the owner' holding one question (close, re-scope or proceed) that recommends the verdict; status is awaiting-owner-decisions and check_spec.py exits 0. No comment, label or issue-body edit is made.

turns.setup: Separate issue asks for a per-run override that skips the scope check for urgent issues. The existing checklist enforces the opposite behavior; there is no evidence that it already serves the requested override. No other cited close or re-scope reason is established.

expectedBehavior.description: Do not call the override redundant merely because both requests mention the scope check. Verdict prd: stages 02-06 run and the override's authority question goes to the owner. No triage-stop spec.

failureShape.observedFailure: Before this stage existed, every issue went straight from read-issue to context-completeness with nothing challenging the ask itself, so a request for a second mechanism serving an already-met need would sail through to a full PRD and, eventually, a second gate/config/flag duplicating one that already worked.
failureShape.note: Must fail against the pre-#169 straight-to-PRD behavior and pass once a citable existing mechanism turns into a triage spec at stage 01b with a named mechanism, never a guessed one.
